body:
Problem: No (public) way to check if cascade is in action.

Solution: Add `v:cascading` variable.

---

A follow up to [this comment](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41657#issuecomment-6078981198).

Decided to go with Vim's approach of "integer with 0 meaning `false`", since there doesn't seem to be a precedent of using "true" booleans `v:true` / `v:false` (if this is even possible).

comment_data.body:
or we could just update the existing "basic" test

```suggestion
  it('v:cascading', function()
```
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -4171,4 +4171,35 @@ describe('multicursor', function()
       eq({ 'aa', 'b' }, get_lines())
     end)
   end)
+
+  describe('v:cascading', function()
+    it('is set during cascade', function()

comment_data.body:
use `set_vim_var_bool` to set a boolean.
```suggestion
  set_vim_var_bool(VV_CASCADING, 1);
```

The initial comment has this:

> Decided to go with Vim's approach of "integer with 0 meaning `false`", since there doesn't seem to be a precedent of using "true" booleans `v:true` / `v:false` (if this is even possible).

Still okay to use boolean?
boolean v: vars that use integer simply existed before Vim had `v:true` / `v:false`, I would not consider it a precedent.

comment_regular_data.body:
oh, now I remember the other problem with `v:` : it cannot (elegantly) be made to work with `api-fast`. That's the main reason why I was resigned to expose it as `nvim_get_mode().cascading` . Or via `state()` maybe.

Other things to look out for:


- Insert-mode live-preview reports "false". (`mc_ins_preview_set` runs outside the "sandbox").
    - This would affect an `on_bytes` listener.
- Visual mode may report "true" when nothing is cascading. `mc_vsel_refresh()` goes through `mc_sandbox_enter`.

> oh, now I remember the other problem with `v:` : it cannot (elegantly) be made to work with `api-fast`. That's the main reason why I was resigned to expose it as `nvim_get_mode().cascading` . Or via `state()` maybe.

I don't feel qualified enough to make a choice here, I am afraid. Is being usable during `api-fast` important here? If yes, then I'd ask for direction, please. Mostly because I don't really like either from the design perspective:

- Diverging `nvim_get_mode()` even more from `vim.fn.mode()` feels wrong.
- Using `state()` might have conflicts with later Vim patches and there is no good character for this (`M` for multicursor, `C` for cascading?).

> Other things to look out for:

As far as I can tell, this (what currently is `v:cascading`) behaves exactly like the current `nvim__mcursor_cascading()`. Not sure doing anything more is wise (without use case and testing).

Off topic for this PR, just commenting:

>  Diverging `nvim_get_mode()` even more from `vim.fn.mode()` feels wrong.

We can just soft-deprecate `vim.fn.mode()`, it's redundant.

>  Using `state()` might have conflicts with later Vim patches and there is no good character for this (`M` for multicursor, `C` for cascading?).

`state()` is very low-level and we aren't going to adopt any more such changes from Vim; we fully own the editor lifecycle now. Things like `SafeState` are half-baked and go in the wrong direction.

> > oh, now I remember the other problem with `v:` : it cannot (elegantly) be made to work with `api-fast`. That's the main reason why I was resigned to expose it as `nvim_get_mode().cascading` . Or via `state()` maybe.
> 
> I don't feel qualified enough to make a choice here, I am afraid. Is being usable during `api-fast` important here?

@justinmk, it would be *really* useful for 0.13 to have some established public way of checking if multicursor is currently cascading. I can adjust this PR to any of two other proposed methods (`vim.api.nvim_get_mode().cascading` or `vim.fn.state('C') ~= ''`).

From the usability UX, for me it goes `if vim.v.cascading` > `if vim.api.nvim_get_mode().cascading` > `if vim.fn.state('C') ~= ''`.
From performance, it seems that `vim.v` has less overhead, while two others compute data for all of their output fields.
Changing `nvim_get_mode()` will come with more churn in tests. *Probably* there'll be some churn for `state()`.

I'm fine with this, we can always add `nvim_get_mode().cascading` later if a non-blocking RPC use-case demands it.
